chapterNote: A short prayer from far away — 'from the end of the earth I call to You' — and the source of one of the church's best-loved lines: lead me to the rock that is higher than I. David is at the edge: of the land, of his strength, of his own heart, which is fainting. He asks to be led up onto a rock he cannot climb by himself, and then he names what God has already been — a shelter, a strong tower — and asks for what he wants most: to be a guest in God's tent forever, hidden under His wings. The middle verse turns on a vow God has already heard and an inheritance already given: the possession that belongs to those who fear His name. Then the psalm prays for the king — add days to his days, let his years run on like generations, let him sit before God forever with covenant love and faithfulness posted as his guard. Christian readers have never been able to pray those lines without thinking of the King whose years actually do run on forever. It ends where vows end: with music to the Name, and the vows paid day by day.

1.text: For the choir director, on a stringed instrument. Of David. Hear my ringing cry, O God; pay attention to my prayer.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] upon Neginah [neginah — a stringed instrument], A Psalm of David. Hear [shama] my cry [rinnah — ringing cry], O God [Elohim]; attend [qashab — listen closely] unto my prayer [tephillah].
1.notes: shimah Elohim rinnati (H8085, H430, H7440): hear, O God, my ringing cry — rinnah is the ringing cry, of joy elsewhere, of need here — haqshibah tephillati (H7181, H8605): listen closely. Verse 1 asks for two ears; verse 2 will say how far away the voice is.

2.text: From the end of the earth I call to You, as my heart is fainting away; lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
2.amp: From the end [qatseh] of the earth [eretz] will I cry [qara] unto You, when my heart [leb] is overwhelmed [ataph — faints, wraps itself in weakness]: lead [nachah] me to the rock [tsur] that is higher [rum] than I.
2.notes: mi-qtseh ha-aretz elekha eqra (H7097, H776, H7121): from the end of the earth — exile, or the far edge of the kingdom, or simply the far edge of himself — ba-atoph libbi (H5848, H3820), as the heart faints. Then the line the church has long sung: be-tsur-yarum mimmenni tancheni (H6697, H7311, H5148) — lead me to a rock too high for me to climb alone; nachah, the shepherd-verb of Psalm 23:3.

3.text: For You have been a shelter for me, a strong tower against the enemy.
3.amp: For You have been a shelter [machseh — refuge] for me, and a strong [oz] tower [migdal] from [panim] the enemy [oyeb].
3.notes: ki-hayita machseh li (H4268): You HAVE BEEN a shelter for me — past experience as the ground of the request — migdal-oz mi-pne oyeb (H4026, H5797, H6440, H341): a strong tower from the enemy's face, Proverbs 18:10's tower, which is the Name.

4.text: Let me be a guest in Your tent forever; let me take refuge in the hiding place of Your wings. Selah.
4.amp: I will abide [gur — sojourn as a guest] in Your tabernacle [ohel — tent] for ever [olam]: I will trust ['make my refuge', chasah — take refuge, the KJV margin] in the covert [sether — hiding place] of Your wings [kanaph]. Selah [selah].
4.notes: agurah be-oholkha olamim (H1481, H168, H5769): gur, the sojourner's verb of Psalm 15:1 — a guest in God's tent, but forever — echeseh be-seter kenaphekha (H2620, H5643, H3671): refuge in the hiding place of Your wings — the sheltering bird of Psalm 17:8 and 91:4, or, set beside 'Your tent', the cherubim's wings over the ark. The far end of the earth (v. 2) asking for the center of the sanctuary.

5.text: For You, O God, have heard my vows; You have given me the inheritance of those who fear Your name.
5.amp: For You, O God [Elohim], have heard [shama] my vows [neder]: You have given [natan] me the heritage [yerushshah — possession] of those that fear [yare] Your name [shem].
5.notes: ki-attah Elohim shamata li-nedarai (H430, H8085, H5088): the vows made in trouble have been heard — natatta yerushshat yire shemekha (H5414, H3425, H3373, H8034): You have given the yerushshah, the possession, that belongs to those who fear Your name. Land and kingdom first, in the Psalter's own idiom (Psalm 25:12-13; 37:11) — but the fearers' deeper inheritance is God Himself (cf. Psalm 16:5).

6.text: Add days to the days of the king; let his years run on like generation after generation.
6.amp: You will prolong ['Thou shalt add days to the days of the king', yasaph, the KJV margin] the king's [melek] life [yom]: and his years [shanah] as many generations ['as generation and generation', dor va-dor, the KJV margin].
6.notes: yamim al-yeme-melekh tosiph (H3117, H4428, H3254): the margin's literal is 'Thou shalt add days to the days of the king' — an imperfect that the psalm's petitionary frame (v. 7's 'appoint') lets us pray rather than predict: add days onto the days of the king — shenotav kemo-dor va-dor (H8141, H1755): his years like generation upon generation. David praying for himself in the third person, and the church praying it for the Son of David, whose years do run on forever (cf. Psalm 21:4; Hebrews 7:16).

7.text: May he sit enthroned before God forever; appoint covenant love and faithfulness to guard him.
7.amp: He shall abide [yashab — sit enthroned, dwell] before [panim] God [Elohim] for ever [olam]: O prepare [manah — appoint, assign] mercy [chesed — covenant love] and truth [emeth], which may preserve [natsar — guard] him.
7.notes: yeshev olam liphne Elohim (H3427, H5769, H6440, H430): sit forever before God's face — the throne next to the throne. chesed ve-emet man yintseruhu (H2617, H571, H4487, H5341): APPOINT covenant love and faithfulness — manah is the assigning-verb, as of a guard detail — to keep watch over him. The king's bodyguard is a pair of divine attributes.

8.text: So I will make music to Your name forever, paying my vows day after day.
8.amp: So will I sing [zamar — make music] praise unto Your name [shem] for ever [ad], that I may daily [yom yom] perform [shalam — pay in full] my vows [neder].
8.notes: ken azammerah shimkha la-ad (H2167, H8034, H5703): SO — on that basis — I will make music to the Name forever, le-shallemi nedarai yom yom (H7999, H5088, H3117): paying the vows of verse 5, day by day. Forever, delivered in daily installments, as in Psalm 145:2.
